newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
BIHAR FODDER SCAM SEIZURES TOUCH ONE BLN RUPEES
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has recovered gold, attached property and seized documents worth upto one billion rupees from some of the accused in the 10 billion rupee Bihar fodder scam.
The CBI, which released reports about significant progress made in the probe into the scam, said little about Bihar chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav's role in the scandal.

CBI sources said the probe into the Bihar animal husbandry case had led to the attachment of property worth over 0.5 billion rupees. The attached property allegedly belonged to 13 of the accused, including two state legislators.
The Hindustan Times
FRESH MOVE ON TO DEFER CONGRESS PARLIAMENTARY PARTY POLLS
A move was afoot in Congress circles for postponement of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) polls, scheduled to be held on December 10.

It seemed to have been initiated amid growing demand from Members of Parliament (MPs) that they should be linked to the election of a new leader of the CPP in place of former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao.

A group of MPs close to Maharashtra leader Sharad Pawar said they would convey to the Congress Chief Whip and other CPP officials their feeling that Rao should step down in the interest of party unity.
The Congress MPs also plan to meet party president Sitaram Kesri in the next two days to demand the postponement of the polls and Narasimha Rao's exit as the CPP leader.
The Economic Times
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX JUMPS 149 POINTS FROM INTRA-DAY LOW

Pivotals rebounded after a sharp retreat on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). The BSE sensitive index (sensex) crossed the 3,000 mark and scaled an intra-day high of 3,004.83, gaining 148.82 points from the intra-day low.

The sensex closed at 2,994.98, showing a net gain of 29.32 points. The broadbased BSE National Index recorded a net gain of 6.93 points. The unusual upswing from intra-day lower levels was largely attributed to sustained purchases by foreign institutional investors coupled with hectic short covering.
The fall and rise were accompanied with huge volumes at 3.66 billion rupees, as against a daily average of three billion rupees.
ONLENDING TO LIVEN UP INTER-BANK FOREX MARKET

The central bank (RBI) move to allow banks to onlend their inter-bank foreign currency borrowings as foreign currency loans to Indian corporates is likely to activate the foreign currency inter-bank market.
Banking sources said corporates were enquiring about foreign currency non-resident FCNR(B) loans with banks which were short of FCNR(B) deposits.

So the banks were looking toward the interbank market as a source of foreign currency, which they could onlend to corporates, sources added. The interest rate on these foreign currency loans will, however, be higher as the cost of funds of these banks is more than banks with large FCNR(B) deposits.
PAYMENTS TO OIL MAJOR TEMPORARILY SUSPENDED
The government temporarily suspended payments to Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) for its crude sales due to the huge oil pool account deficit.

The move came as finance minister P. Chidambaram virtually ruled out all options but a price hike. The government also cut weekly settlements to all refining-cum-marketing companies including Indian Oil Corporation.
Official sources said the government had decided to give preference to refining companies, whose sole source of financing was the Oil Coordination Committee.
ITC REKINDLED, NET INCREASES 28 PCT

ITC Ltd showed a 28 percent spurt in unaudited net profit for the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). The company board also unanimously decided to induct two independent non-executive directors.
Profit after tax and depreciation rose to 1.81 billion rupees from 1.41 billion rupees during the corresponding period last fiscal and 2.61 billion rupees for 1995/96.

The gross income of the company touched 29.06 billion rupees as compared to 25.02 billion rupees during the corresponding period last fiscal, indicating that the tobacco giant is well on its way to touch a turnover of 60 billion rupees during 1996/97.
Financial Express
ELECTRICAL SECTOR REELING UNDER LOW GROWTH RATE
Many sectors of the electrical industry registered a low growth rate of less than eight percent in production during the first six months of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).
The Indian Electrical and Electronics Manufacturers' Association said sectors such as transmission towers, large transformers and energy meters had already started showing negative growth rates.
Transmission towers registered a negative growth rate of eight percent during the first six months of the current fiscal.
Production of transformers slumped with an overall negative growth rate of five percent. Energy meters exhibited a negative growth rate of five percent during the period.
